name: Wasmtime
summary: An embeddable WebAssembly runtime that separates shared compilation context from store-scoped instance state, compiles modules through validation and parallel function compilation, and enters JIT code through typed trampolines.

features.name: Engine and store state boundary
features.description: Wasmtime uses an Engine as a shared compilation context and a Store as the container and isolation unit for WebAssembly objects such as instances, globals, memories, and tables. Objects from different stores do not interact through the Wasmtime object model.
benefits: Allows compiled artifacts and type interning to be shared through an Engine
Provides a clear lifetime and isolation boundary for instantiated objects
costs: Objects are store-affine and cannot be freely moved across stores
Engine synchronization and store lifetime rules add embedding constraints

features.name: Validated parallel module compilation
features.description: Module compilation first validates the module and builds an environment descriptor, then validates and compiles functions in parallel, collects inert compilation artifacts, and finally maps code into executable memory before producing a compiled Module.
benefits: Separates validation, function compilation, artifact assembly, and executable publication
Allows independent function compilation work to proceed in parallel
costs: Compilation requires several intermediate artifacts and publication steps
Function-level compilation without inter-procedural analysis limits some optimization opportunities

features.name: Typed host-to-WebAssembly entry boundary
features.description: Wasmtime generates trampolines for exported function signatures so a host call with a known ABI can enter JIT code compiled with a different native function signature. Instantiation type-checks imports before creating the instance state.
benefits: Hides native ABI differences from the embedding API
Makes import and call compatibility checks explicit at the runtime boundary
costs: Trampolines add generated code and signature-management work
Host and guest values remain constrained by WebAssembly type matching

mathematical_views.question: How do Engine-level shared state, Store-level ownership, and instance lifecycle transitions constrain WebAssembly execution?
assumptions: Engine, Store, Module, and Instance are modeled as state components with explicit ownership edges
Store affinity is treated as an invariant for WebAssembly objects
The view abstracts allocator implementation details and host scheduling

mathematical_views.question: Which stages must a WebAssembly module pass before compiled code can be instantiated and called?
assumptions: Validation, function compilation, artifact assembly, executable mapping, and instantiation are ordered transitions
The compiled artifact is inert until the executable publication stage
The view describes the documented pipeline and does not prove performance or complete implementation equivalence

benefits: Shared compilation resources with store-scoped isolation
costs: Store affinity and synchronization rules constrain embedding design

benefits: Parallel compilation and an explicit executable-publication boundary
costs: Intermediate artifacts and limited inter-procedural analysis add complexity

benefits: Stable host call boundary despite guest function ABI variation
costs: Signature checking and trampoline generation add runtime and compilation surface
